chain.label: Night darkness at STL
chain.trigger: the accident occurred ... during the hours of darkness

chain.label: Cessna pilot operating past his normal rest time
chain.trigger: the accident occurred at a time of night when the pilot normally went to sleep, and he may have been tired

chain.label: ATIS omitted occasional runway 31 departure use
chain.trigger: No mention was made of the occasional use of runway 31 as a departure runway in this ATIS recording

chain.label: Ground controller issued nonstandard, incomplete taxi clearance
chain.trigger: back-taxi into position hold runway three one ... the phrase 'taxi to,' and the departure runway had been eliminated

chain.label: Cessna pilot's preconception overrode the actual runway-31 clearance
chain.trigger: the pilot had a preconception that he would be departing on runway 30R and thus did not register the ground controller's clearance to runway 31

caused_by.evidence: operating during a period in which he was normally at rest may have had some effect on his ... attentiveness
if runway 31 had been referenced ... on the ATIS broadcast, the pilot may have been more attentive
Had the taxi clearance been in accordance with prescribed phraseology, it might have altered the pilot's preconception

chain.label: Cessna pilot omitted runway assignment from his clearance readback
chain.trigger: the Cessna pilot did not state the departure runway in any of his clearance readbacks

caused_by.evidence: did not register the ground controller's clearance to runway 31

chain.label: Cessna pilot taxied onto and held in position on runway 30R instead of runway 31
chain.trigger: his mistaken belief that his assigned departure runway was runway 30R, which resulted in his undetected entrance onto runway 30R

caused_by.evidence: mistaken belief that his assigned departure runway was runway 30R

chain.label: ASDE-3 surface radar unavailable due to computer hard drive failure
chain.trigger: The ASDE-3 equipment was not available for controller reference on the night of the accident due to a computer hard drive failure

chain.label: Controllers failed to detect Cessna 441 on runway 30R and cleared MD-82 for takeoff
chain.trigger: the local controller cleared the MD-82 for takeoff on runway 30R ... the ground and local controllers could not have reasonably been expected to visually detect the Cessna pilot's deviation

caused_by.evidence: difficult to see small airplanes operating on the north side of the airport ... at night
had the ASDE-3 equipment been available ... the controllers would have had a higher probability of identifying the Cessna 441

chain.label: MD-82 flightcrew did not see Cessna 441 until seconds before impact
chain.trigger: they did not observe the airplane or airplane position lights at any point during their takeoff roll ... they first saw the airplane when it was illuminated by the lights from the MD-82

caused_by.evidence: the local controller cleared the MD-82 for takeoff on runway 30R

chain.label: MD-82 collided with Cessna 441 at the runway 30R/taxiway Romeo intersection
chain.trigger: the right wing of the MD-82 struck the tail cone and fuselage structure of the Cessna 441

caused_by.evidence: About 2 to 3 seconds after the flightcrew saw the Cessna 441, they felt an impact
undetected entrance onto runway 30R, which was being used by the MD-82 for its departure

chain.label: Cessna 441 pilot and pilot-rated passenger killed
chain.trigger: The commercial pilot and the passenger ... were the sole occupants on board the Cessna and were killed

caused_by.evidence: This accident was not survivable for the occupants of the Cessna
